terms.meaning: Local bodies elected by local people to solve local problems. It decentralises power.
The village council of all villagers aged 18 and above. It has no election.
Panchayat Development Officer, appointed by the state to run a Grama Panchayat with its secretary.
The executive head, of District Commissioner rank. Attends meetings but can't vote.
Head of a City Corporation and the "First citizen" of the city, elected by corporators for one year.
The real executive of a City Corporation, usually from the IAS.

items.name: Laws behind local government
items.formula: British Acts of 1919 and 1935; the 73rd and 74th Amendments came into force in 1993.
items.example: The goal was Gandhiji's Grama Swarajya.

items.name: Panchayat Raj in Karnataka
items.formula: The 1983 Act set up Zilla Parishats and Mandal Panchayats; the 1993 Act made the three-tier Panchayat Raj.

items.name: Aims of local self government
items.formula: Involve local people, teach them administration, decentralise power, build local leaders.
items.example: Problems are solved at the local level.

items.name: Income of rural local bodies
items.formula: Cesses (water, health, education, library), building and land taxes, rents, and state grants.
items.example: Tourist spots can also be taxed.

items.name: Grama Sabha meetings
items.formula: At least once in six months, chaired by the Grama Panchayat president.
items.example: It recommends who should get government schemes.

items.name: Grama Panchayat
items.formula: Population 5,000 to 7,000 (2,000 in Uttara Kannada, Dakshina Kannada and Malnad); one member for 400 voters.
items.example: Term 5 years; Adhyaksha and Upadhyaksha for 30 months; meets at least once in two months.

items.name: Toilet rule for panchayat members
items.formula: From the 2000 amendment, a member must have a toilet at home, or build one within one year.
items.example: A third of members must be present to decide.

items.name: Taluk Panchayat
items.formula: One member per 10,000 voters; a fifth of Grama Panchayat presidents join by lot for a year.
items.example: Run by an executive officer; it combines the gram panchayats' plans for the Zilla Panchayat.

items.name: Zilla Panchayat
items.formula: One member per 40,000 people (30,000 in the coastal and Chikkamagaluru districts, 18,000 in Kodagu).
items.example: Its Adhyaksha can sanction one lakh rupees for disaster relief; it has 5 standing committees.

items.name: State Election Commission
items.formula: Set up under Articles 243K and 243ZA (73rd and 74th Amendments).
items.example: It holds panchayat and urban body elections.

items.name: Town and City Municipalities
items.formula: Town: 20,000 to 50,000 people, 23 to 27 councillors. City: 50,000 to 3 lakh, 31 to 37 councillors.
items.example: The state nominates 5 more members who can't vote; the Chief Officer is the head of administration.

items.name: City Corporation (Mahanagara Palike)
items.formula: Over two lakh people and an income above one crore rupees; 30 to 100 corporators.
items.example: Karnataka has 11: 10 city corporations and BBMP, which has 225 wards.

items.name: Income of urban bodies
items.formula: Taxes on buildings, sites, shops and carts; rents; cesses; state grants.
items.example: Water, market and entertainment cesses add revenue.

mistakes.text: The Grama Sabha has no election: every adult villager is a member. The Grama Panchayat is elected.
The 73rd Amendment is for panchayats (rural); the 74th is for urban local bodies.
Panchayat presidents serve 30 months, but mayors and municipal presidents serve one year. Members serve 5 years.
